subtopics.title: The Cast of Symbols and the Four Equations

questions.question: The equations of motion may only be used when:
options: The object moves in a circle

questions.question: Which quantity is missing from the equation vf² = vi² + 2aΔx?
The 'absent character' rule for choosing an equation says:
options: Pick the equation with the most symbols
Pick the equation you remember best
Pick the equation that excludes the quantity which is neither given nor wanted

subtopics.title: Choosing the Equation and Finding the Acceleration

questions.question: For the car problem (vi = 10 m/s, vf = 25 m/s, Δx = 300 m, find a), the absent quantity is:
options: Displacement — so use vf = vi + aΔt
Initial velocity — so use equation two

questions.question: Substituting into vf² = vi² + 2aΔx gives 625 = 100 + 600a. The acceleration is:
options: 0,875 m/s² in the direction of motion

questions.question: Why must the direction be stated with the acceleration answer?

subtopics.title: Finding the Time — Two Roads to One Answer

questions.question: Using vf = vi + aΔt with a = 0,875 m/s², the time taken is:
The check via Δx = ½(vi + vf)Δt uses the average velocity, which is:
Why is the second road (equation four) such a strong check on the first?
options: It uses only original given data, so an error in the calculated acceleration could not hide
It always gives a slightly different answer

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: A car travels at 90 km/h. Before using the equations of motion, this must become:
In vf² = vi² + 2aΔx, a common error is:
options: Forgetting to square the velocities — writing 25 instead of 625

questions.question: If the car had been braking, the acceleration in your equations would be:
options: Negative (opposite to the chosen positive direction of motion)

questions.question: In Grade 12, these same equations reappear in vertical projectile motion, where the constant acceleration is:
options: Zero at the top of the flight
Different for heavy and light objects

questions.question: The five facts that describe any straight-line trip are:
options: Distance, mass, time, speed and force
Starting speed, final speed, acceleration, time and displacement
Speed, velocity, distance, displacement and direction
Time, fuel, distance, mass and acceleration

questions.question: The word 'uniformly' in a question is important because:
options: It means the car is travelling on a straight road
It means the speed never changes
It tells you the distance is exact
It is your permission to use the equations at all — the acceleration must be steady

questions.question: An acceleration of 0,875 m/s² means, in plain words:
options: The car travels 0,875 metres each second
The car gains 0,875 metres per second of extra speed in each second
The car takes 0,875 seconds to stop
The car's speed is 0,875 of its top speed

questions.question: Which equation has NO acceleration in it?
options: Final speed equals starting speed plus acceleration times time
Final speed squared equals starting speed squared plus two times acceleration times distance
Distance equals the average of the two speeds times the time
Distance equals starting speed times time plus half the acceleration times time squared

subtopics.title: The One Fact You Don't Need

questions.question: In the car problem, which fact does nobody mention and nobody ask for?
After substituting, 625 = 100 + 600 × acceleration. The next step is:
options: Subtract 100 from both sides, then divide by 600

questions.question: Why does 0,875 m/s² pass the sense check while 87 m/s² would not?
options: Because answers must be less than 1
Because 87 is not a round number
Because gaining just under a metre per second of speed each second is an ordinary pull-away

questions.question: The plain-language choosing rule is:
options: Use the equation with the most given values in it
Find the fact nobody mentioned, then take the equation that leaves it out
Try each equation until one works

questions.question: The car goes smoothly from 10 m/s to 25 m/s, so its average speed for the trip is:
Using 300 m = 17,5 m/s × time, the time taken is:
Why is the change-counting comparison a good description of the two roads?
options: Two independent counts that agree are worth far more than one confident count
Because money and motion use the same formula
Because you should always divide twice
Because the second road is quicker

questions.question: Ninety kilometres per hour is 90 000 metres in 3 600 seconds, which is:
options: 25 m/s — which is why you divide km/h by 3,6
